newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up 5.35 pct in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up 5.35 pct in active trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed up 5.35 percent in heavy trade on Friday on speculative buying after Beijing's announcement that the yuan would be convertible under the current account from December 1, brokers said.
The B index surged 7.25 points to 142.71, with turnover rising to HK$348.97 million from HK$231.16 million on Thursday.
The announcement on yuan convertibility is an indication that the day is approaching when China formally lifts the ban on domestic investors buying hard currency B shares, brokers said.
The market should move up next week but will fluctuate in a wide range, one analyst said.

A surge in Changan Automobile in heavy trade helped market sentiment, brokers said. Changan, the best performer, rose HK$0.41, or 12.24 percent, to HK$3.76 in the most active trade of 14.81 million shares on institutional demand, brokers said.
Beverage maker Shenbao jumped HK$0.47, or 11.60 percent, to HK$4.52 on volume of 690,618 shares on speculative buying.
China Bicycle registered trade of 6.15 million shares to close up HK$0.30, or ten percent, at HK$3.30. Dadonghai climbed HK$0.41 to HK$3.76, with 6.89 million shares changing hands.
Konka was the sole loser, slipping HK$0.08 to HK$7.90, on thin volume of 140,050 shares.

The A market rebounded modestly after falls for three straight sessions, edging up 2.72 points, or 0.61 percent, to 445.42. Turnover was 9.29 billion yuan compared with the previous session's 9.61 billion.
The composite index finished up 3.39 points, or 0.81 percent, at 419.64.
Some investors are diverting money to the Shanghai market, which has performed worse than Shenzhen over the past few months, brokers said.
Chinese premier Li Peng's visit to Shanghai this week fueled speculative buying of Shanghai-listed shares, they said.

Guangdong Fenghua Advanced Technology Holdings Co Ltd, which listed 12.15 million A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, ended the session at 23.90 yuan each against a recent offer price of 8.50 yuan per share.
